key_insight: A combined CEL simulation and ANN framework can accurately predict temperature, axial force, and defect formation in HDPE friction stir welding, enabling fast identification of robust processing windows.
engineering_relevance: The study provides practical process maps for selecting rotation speed, welding speed, and bottom preheating to reduce wormhole defects and stabilize welding forces in thermoplastic joining.
method: 3D Coupled Eulerian-Lagrangian (CEL) finite-element model of HDPE FSW
Two multilayer perceptron ANNs trained on experimental thermal and force signals
Validation against experiments and generation of defect/no-defect process windows
evidence_signal: The ANN models achieved R² values between 0.91 and 0.99, and the CEL model matched experimental void formation, thermal response, and force trends.
watch_item: The workflow was validated on a limited experimental parameter space, so broader material grades, tool geometries, and thicknesses may require retraining and revalidation.
paper_title: Computational and machine learning modelling approaches for weld quality predictions in friction stir welding of high-density polyethylene
